corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science records, large language models appear as both research instruments and social actors. The corpus shows methodological uses of LLMs in policy analysis, education, health communication, and sentiment analysis, alongside deepening attention to human–AI interaction, trust, and embodiment. Recurring concerns include bias, misinformation, ethical governance, and the gap between algorithmic and situated knowledge, with emphasis on governance, literacy, and responsible deployment.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools in social science
themes.description: Papers demonstrate LLMs aiding data classification, content analysis, ethics review, and simulation across policy, health, climate, and education, while highlighting validation and transparency needs.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies investigate trust, perceived humanness, addiction, embodiment, and adoption of AI across health, education, media, and everyday contexts.

themes.name: AI in health communication, wellbeing, and misinformation
themes.description: Works examine AI’s role in health information dissemination, patient education, misinformation mitigation, and wellbeing outcomes.

themes.name: AI in education, literacy, and assessment
themes.description: Research covers AI tutoring, classroom integration, assessment integrity, teacher perspectives, and strategies to foster AI literacy and safe AI-enabled learning.
